value: irrational unless n is an mth power
note: standard result
solution: The \(m\)th root of a natural number is an integer when the number is a perfect \(m\)th power, and irrational otherwise. So \(\sqrt[m]{n}\) is irrational unless \(n\) is the \(m\)th power of an integer.
